candidates.change_summary: Remove the overflow/underflow assert so deposit only increments balance without the assert check.
Invert the assert to assert that addition does not increase balance (will typically revert), changing observable outcome after deposit.
Move the balances increment before the assert, causing the assert to check the post-increment condition and potentially behave differently.
Replace the addition with subtraction so deposit reduces stored balance by msg.value, changing observable balance after deposit.
Ignore msg.value and set the balance to msg.value instead of incrementing, so deposit overwrites previous balance.
Swap the order of transfer and balance decrement so transfer happens after decreasing the internal balance (prevents reentrancy exploit variants and changes observable post-withdraw balance).
Subtract a fixed value (1) from the stored balance after transfer, changing the remaining balance observed after withdraw.
After transferring the requested amount, set the caller's balance to zero instead of decreasing by the withdrawn amount, altering post-withdraw balance observable.
Omit the balance decrement entirely so balances remain unchanged after a successful withdraw, changing observable state.
Decrease the balance by a larger amount (double the requested amount), causing the stored balance after withdraw to differ and potentially revert on underflow (changed behavior under 0.8).
